newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - France's Canal Plus profits jump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - France's Canal Plus profits jump.

text.p: French pay televison company Canal Plus, due to merge with Swiss-controlled Nethold to become Europe's biggest subscription televison group, said on Tuesday its first half net profits rose 16.6 percent.
The company warned start-up costs of its French digital satellite televison venture launched in April would weigh on results although full-year earnings would be at least equal to 1995's.

Canal Plus said in a statement its net attributable profit for the first half rose to 386 million francs ($75.33 million) from 331 million last year. In 1995, the group posted a full year net attributable figure of 665.8 million.
The company published its figures shortly before the Paris Bourse closed after a source close to the company gave Reuters the first half results and profit forecast.
Canal Plus, whose supervisory board met on Tuesday, had planned to publish the figures after the bourse closed.

It shares firmed sharply on the leaked figure, which was in line with analyst forecasts. The stock rose 28 francs to the day's high of 1,219 francs before giving back some of the gains. The share, which had been trading 12 francs higher at 1,207 just before the news, closed at the same level.

"The good financial and commercial health of the parent company, the improvement of the contribution of foreign subsidiaries and the turnaround of the situation at Studio Canal Plus should continue in the second half," Canal Plus said.

"However, while the start-up costs of the digital services in April only affect two months of the first half results, they will in full on the second half. Taking account of these various elements and the seasonality of our sales, the group Canal Plus expects for 1996 a net attributable figure at least equal to that of 1995."

Sales increased 8.3 percent to 5.44 billion francs and Canal Plus said the launch of digital services had boosted the number of subscribers to Canalsatellite by 85 percent to a level "much higher than our initial estimates."
Its French television unit saw its operating margin rise to 26.1 percent from 21.2 percent a year ago.
Canal Plus took a 31 million exceptional charge to provide against the risk of "certain participations" without giving any details.

Market sources said that main Canal Plus shareholder, Havas, was planning to buy up to 10 percent more shares, at a maximum price of 1,200 francs per share, to counter the dilution of its stake following the Nethold merger.
But Havas said it had not bought Canal Plus shares on the market and "was not in the market to buy the share."

"The Societe Generale has obtained a mandate to buy Canal Plus shares for Havas up to a limit of 1,200 francs," per share, one source said. Another source said "Societe Generale could buy up to 10 percent of Canal Plus for Havas."
After the planned merger with Nethold, Havas will have 17.3 percent instead of 23.65 percent while Generale des Eaux will hold 15.4 percent instead of 20.4.
On Friday, Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert bought a 1.33 percent stake in Canal Plus from Paribas. ($1=5.124 French Franc)
